report.source_text: On examination, uncorrected visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/20 OS. Anterior segment was within normal limits in both the eyes on slit-lamp examination, including intraocular pressure (IOP). Relative afferent pupillary defect was present in the right eye. Patient could identify 24/24 plates of a standard Ishihara chart with increased latency OD. Confrontational visual fields revealed an inferior visual field defect in the right eye.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Parainfectious optic neuritis following COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old healthy woman presented with acute-onset blurring of vision and inferior absolute scotoma in the right eye for 4 days, preceded by viral prodrome (fever, sore throat, fatigue) 10 days prior and laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 exposure 15 days prior. Clinical examination revealed right optic nerve dysfunction with relative afferent pupillary defect, dyschromatopsia with increased latency, and inferior altitudinal visual field defect. Fundoscopy demonstrated papillitis with nasal, superior, and inferior disc margin blurring and vascular tortuosity. MRI brain and spine were within normal limits, excluding demyelinating disease. RT-PCR testing confirmed active COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1g daily for 3 days) followed by oral prednisolone, with documented resolution of disc edema during admission and subjective resolution of the inferior scotoma at 3-week telephonic follow-up.

MRI brain and spine within normal limits without demyelinating lesions
